cards.title: 1-0-1 is not a phone number
cards.body: It's the most common code on Indian prescriptions, and it's simpler than it looks. Three numbers, three times of day.

cards.title: Morning, afternoon, night
cards.body: First number is morning, middle is afternoon, last is night. So 1-0-1 means one in the morning, none in the afternoon, one at night.

cards.title: Same logic, other patterns
cards.body: 1-1-1 is three times a day. 0-0-1 is night only. 1-0-0 is morning only. The number tells you how many tablets.

cards.title: Halves show up too
cards.body: ½-0-½ means half a tablet in the morning and half at night. Ask the chemist whether that tablet can be split safely.

cards.title: Unclear? Ask before the first dose
cards.body: Some doctors add a fourth slot or food notes. If anything looks odd, ask the pharmacist, then write the timings in plain words on the strip.

takeaway: In 1-0-1, the numbers stand for morning, afternoon and night doses. Ask your pharmacist if a pattern looks unclear.
share: Send this to the cousin who thought 1-0-1 was a room number.
